 1.1 Process of Data Communication and Its Components  
 
Data Communication – Definition  
Data communication  is the process of exchanging data or information between two or more 
devices  through a communication medium  such as cables, optical fiber, or wireless signals.  
The data may include:  
• Text  
• Numbers  
• Images (graphics)  
• Audio  
• Video  
 The primary goal of data communication is to deliver data accurately, reliably, and on time . 
 
Objectives of Data Communication  
A successful data communication system must ensure:  
1. Accuracy  
o Data should arrive without errors  
o Errors during transmission must be detected and corrected  
2. Timeliness

3. Reliability  
o System should work consistently

Process of Data Communication  
The process of data communication  involves sending data from a sender  to a receiver  through 
a communication medium , following a set of rules called protocols . 
Basic Flow of Communication  
Sender → Transmission Medium → Receiver  
The communication is considered successful only when:  
• The receiver correctly understands the message sent by the sender  
• Both devices follow the same protocol

 1.3.2 Half Duplex Communication Mode  
Definition  
In half duplex communication mode , data can flow in both directions , but not at the same 
time . 
At any given moment, one device sends data while the other receives.  
Sender ⇄ Receiver (one at a time ) 
 
Characteristics  
• Bidirectional communication  
• Only one direction active at a time  
• Devices take turns to send and receive  
 
Examples  
• Walkie -talkie  
• CB radio  
• Police communication systems

3. WAN – Wide Area Network
